description:

- Minimum two years experience in Customer Service or Sale Support.

If you're interested in this role, apply now!

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Customer Service Advisor- Temporary

Reports to: Branch Manager / Area Operations Manager
Location: Bedford
Department: Customer Service / Operations

Temp role

Our Client is looking for an experienced customer Service Advisor to join their growing team. If you're passionate about delivering exceptional customer service, enjoy building strong customer relationships, and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you.

As part of our ambitious growth strategy, our goal is to triple the number of repeat customers over the next five years. This role is central to achieving that ambition by ensuring every customer receives outstanding service, expert support, and a seamless experience from enquiry through to order fulfilment.

The Role

As a Customer Service Advisor, you'll be the first point of contact for many of our customers, providing a friendly, professional, and efficient service across a broad range of products. You'll process customer orders, manage enquiries, resolve issues, and work closely with colleagues across the business to deliver an outstanding customer experience.

This is a varied role that combines customer service, sales support, administration, and operational collaboration, making it ideal for someone who enjoys taking ownership and making a real difference.

What You'll Be Doing
- Deliver outstanding customer service across phone, email, and other communication channels.
- Process customer orders accurately and efficiently, ensuring prompt fulfilment.
- Handle customer enquiries and provide product guidance and recommendations.
- Escalate technical product enquiries to specialist teams where appropriate.
- Resolve customer issues and complaints professionally, achieving positive outcomes.
- Liaise with internal departments and external stakeholders to ensure smooth order processing.
- Follow up quotations and proactively engage with customers.
- Identify and communicate sales opportunities to the External Sales Team.
- Support branch operations, including warehouse or trade counter activities when required.
- Participate in stock cycle counting.
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance customer experience and operational efficiency.
- Support the wider branch team and undertake additional duties as required.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who enjoys helping customers, takes pride in delivering excellent service, and works well as part of a team.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience in a customer service, sales support, or internal sales role.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Strong organisational skills with great attention to detail.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment.
- A proactive approach to problem solving and customer service.
- Experience using ERP or order processing systems (desirable).
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
- A willingness to develop product knowledge and learn about our industry.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, you'll help ensure:
- Customers receive consistently outstanding service.
- Orders are processed accurately and efficiently.
- Customer enquiries and complaints are resolved quickly and professionally.
- Strong customer relationships are developed and maintained.
- Sales opportunities are identified and passed to the relevant teams.
- The branch achieves improvements in customer retention, sales growth, and operational performance.
- You make a positive contribution to our team culture and business success.

title: Minute taking Business Administrator
description:
Connect 2 Luton are excited to recruit a Minute Taking Administrator i on behalf of Luton Borough Council.

Main purpose of position:

The post holder will provide high level administration support and information to the Strategy, Engagement & Implementation. They will support the management of the Team inbox's to action the tasks according to priority with the aim of improving the quality of data that is recorded on social care systems. They will also provide support to ensure the efficient running of projects. They will support the administration tasks in relation to external suppliers and contribute to the performance management in relation to the key performance indicators set.

As a Business support officer you will be responsible to:
- Undertake and lead on complex administrative tasks in a high volume and deadline driven environment
- Manage specific project support tasks with minimal supervision as part of own workload as required by line management
- Support the management of team email box(s) to ensure action in a timely way ensuring accurate recording
- Ensure data recorded is accurate and concise
- Creation, development and maintenance of records, files and statistical information for evidence based data
- Handle conflicting priorities from managers being aware of public scrutiny and partnership working within LBC and with local stakeholders requiring a high level of professionalism
- Taking on a coordination function between the council and externally commissioned resource to support timely actions and forward planning
- Manage the logistics and administration of all identified project meetings, to include suitable minute taking records, ensuring the division maintain a uniformed communication strategy and information flow across all meetings
- Maintain and collate management information to meet divisional management requirements, and produce periodic reports within defined time-scales to enable management to review performance
- Develop, implement, maintain and monitor administrative systems and procedures to support operational needs of the division, ensure the team is up to date with public information, national and local policies, procedures and strategy
- Be able, and as a nominated responsible officer, to undertake the processing of invoices, and stores requisitions, managing the distribution and the returning of laptops and equipment as and when required , maintaining accurate records
- To participate and where required facilitate working relationships with teams and staff from other divisions to ensure consistency as far as practicable
- Contribute to the maintenance of a healthy, safe, effective working environment, monitoring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements including H&S, property, equipment issues, and IT facilities
- Ensure that relevant corporate and departmental procedures are available and kept up to date

Skills and Experience
- Demonstrable administrative experience including developing, managing and maintaining complex administrative systems and procedures
- Some experience of organising and leading project work
- Previous local authority experience or Social Care setting
- Ability to communicate and build effective relationships with staff and stakeholders in a polite manner at levels
- Ability to write clear letters and reports
- Good IT skills
- Able to use own initiative
- Ability to perform basic calculations and analyse and interpret data
- Excellent administrative and organisational skills
- Able to provide a quality service to customers
- Some understanding of national policy surrounding health and social care
- Education to Level 2 Business management or equivalent experience
- Able to attend meetings and undertake work at various locations throughout the Borough

About Us

Luton Borough Council have partnered with Kent County Council to create Connect 2 Luton, a recruitment managed service for all contingent temporary agency, contract, and interim roles at the Council.

Our heritage and being local government owned which means we have a wealth of knowledge and expertise within the public sector, with many of our employees having previously worked for the Council or have supplied previously into the Council, for several years.

We are an equal opportunities employment agency and business that positively encourages applications from all suitably qualified and eligible candidates.

Connect 2 Luton is an equal opportunities Employment Agency & Business. It positively encourages applications from all suitably qualified and eligible candidates.

title: Supply Chain Administrator
description:
Our client is looking to recruit a Supply Chain Administrator for a 2 month temp position, could go on longer.

Role Purpose

To assist the company in achieving its business objectives and revenue targets by supporting the supply chain activity within the business from order receipt to order dispatch including the purchasing of materials maintaining optimum inventory levels and delivering a high level and professional level of customer service.

Key Responsibilities
- Take responsibility for aspects of inventory control including purchasing of specified items including consumables from material planning phase to final issue, to ensure On Time , On Quality and On Cost delivery is achieved.
- Ensure accurate records are maintained in all areas relating to supply chain activities.
- Daily interface to both internal & external customers and suppliers.
- Manage all material allocations from material requisitions ensuring stock accuracy throughout.
- Enter, process and confirm sales and service orders for customers.
- Respond to emails and answer telephone calls to customers for example and not limited to stock availability, pricing, quotes, pro-forma invoicing, complaints, customs numbers, weights, dimensions and sending duplicate invoices.
- Run invoices for both UK & Export shipments and when required provide export shipping documentation and support to the stores to allow dispatch.
- Support cost improvements by actively perusing total cost reduction opportunities.
- Review inventory to determine unused items or surplus materials.
- Make recommendations and support improvements to supply chain processes and procedures.
- Ensure that all activities are undertaken and controlled in accordance with the Quality Management System (QMS).
- Maintain Key Performance Indicators (KPI s) to measure performance and demonstrate continuous improvement.
- Take responsibility for the stock-takes both annual and perpetual as required.

Work Experience

Essential
- Intermediate experience of MS Office including Excel and Word.
- Excellent communication skills.
- Proven experience of attention to detail, accurate and able to work on own initiative.
- Previous experience working in a stores environment as a material controller or stores supervisor.
- Experience of MRP systems.
- Customer Service Experience
- Export Shipping Experience
- Experience of dealing directly with customers by telephone and email.
- Awareness of health and safety in respect of COSHH and manual handling.

title: Payroll Administrator
company: The Disability Resource Centre - Agency - Permanent
description:
Payroll Administrator

Pay: £17,229.73 - £18,494.59 per year (part-time - 20-25hrs)

About Us

The Disability Resource Centre is an award-winning charity helping people affected by disability or long-term health conditions. We are an independent organisation and a registered charity that has disabled people at the centre of its decision making.

Our Vision

Empowering people of all ages who are affected by disability or health conditions to fulfil their potential and aspirations.

Our Mission

The Disability Resource Centre is here so that disabled people and their families have somewhere to turn if they feel alone and need help in any situation. We want all disabled people, those with long term health conditions and their carers to know that we are here to support them.

About The Role

We are looking for an accurate, organised and customer-focused Payroll Administrator to support our busy Direct Payments payroll service. You will help deliver timely and compliant payroll services for individual employers and Personal Assistants, while providing helpful support by telephone and email.

This is a varied role for someone who is confident managing end-to-end payroll tasks, maintaining clear records and working with employers, service users, HMRC and pension providers

Key responsibilities
- Set up and maintain payroll records for employers, including HMRC registrations, employment information, pension arrangements and payroll files.
- Accurately process weekly and monthly payroll data, including pay, tax, National Insurance, pensions, holiday pay, statutory payments, expenses and deductions.
- Produce and distribute payslips and complete payroll year-end processes and statutory documentation.
- Administer monthly pension contributions and payments through NEST, manage auto-enrolment requirements and submit pension declarations by statutory deadlines.
- Prepare and submit HMRC documentation, including RTI submissions, reports and year-end returns.
- Respond to payroll and finance-related telephone calls, emails and enquiries, providing guidance within agreed boundaries.
- Maintain accurate records for audits and local authority reporting, and support payroll-related invoicing and payment monitoring.
- Work closely with colleagues across Payroll, Direct Payments, Holding Accounts and Finance to maintain an accurate and responsive service.

About You

You will have:
- At least two years' experience working in a busy payroll environment.
- Experience of end-to-end payroll processing.
- Working knowledge of HMRC regulations and payroll systems.
- Strong accuracy, attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Confidence using payroll and finance systems, Excel and digital filing tools.
- A clear understanding of confidentiality and data protection.
- The ability to manage your workload proactively and effectively within a part-time role.
- A commitment to equality, inclusion and the rights of disabled people and carers.

Experience using BrightPay, Xero or NEST, working in a payroll bureau or Direct Payments environment, producing payroll or financial reports, or working in a charity or social enterprise would be desirable.

How To Apply

Please submit your CV together with a cover letter explaining why you are interested in the role and how your experience meets the requirements.

As a Disability Confident Leader, we are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is inclusive and accessible to all. We particularly welcome applications from disabled people, those with long-term health conditions, and people with caring responsibilities.

If you meet the minimum essential criteria for the role and declare a disability, you will be offered a guaranteed interview under our inclusive recruitment policy.

Right to Work in the UK

Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Any offer of employment will be subject to appropriate right to work checks in line with current UK requirements.

Please note: We reserve the right to close this advertisement early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications, as we are keen to appoint as soon as possible.

title: Clinical Research Administrator
company: SPD Development Company Ltd - Agency - Contract
description:
Clinical Research Administrator

Salary: £30,000 to £35,000 depending on skills and experience + Benefits + Bonus

Location: Bedford

The Vacancy

12-month Fixed Term Contract starting January 2027

We are looking for a Clinical Research Administrator to provide support, conduct and monitoring of Clinical studies within the wider Clinical programme ensuring compliance with study protocols and GCP. This will include study preparation, preparation of supplies, volunteer recruitment, study conduct and tracking activities.

SPD (Swiss Precision Diagnostics) are world leaders in the research, design and supply of advanced consumer diagnostic products. SPD is a joint venture business between P&G and Abbott, and our brand Clearblue is recognised the world over as providing accurate home pregnancy and fertility monitoring tests.

In this role you will be contributing and supporting internal Clinical studies which involves:
- Set-up activities, including sourcing study supplies, packaging and shipment of supplies.
- Tracking study status, inputting into study conduct meetings and reporting of study status.
- Contributing to study administration and execution activities volunteer recruitment, printing, collation, packing, payment, source data verification and testing.
- Administering and recording volunteer payments for studies.
- Supporting study team meetings and maintaining inspection-ready documentation.

We are looking for individuals who have:
- Good communication skills, both written and verbal, with excellent telephone skills. Previous experience of telephone work is desirable.
- Excellent attention to detail and must be highly organised.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint and Excel).
- Ideally a Bachelor s Degree in Biomedical Science or a related field.
- Ideally experience with clinical studies.
- Ideally knowledge of IVDR, ISO20916 and ISO13485.
- The personal attributes, attitude and mindset of Results focused, Self-aware and a Team player.

We want you to join us and actively work with colleagues across the business to achieve great things for people in their reproductive life.

We can offer you:
- An excellent working environment
- 25 days paid annual leave plus bank holidays
- Company pension scheme including competitive employer s contribution
- Private Medical Insurance package with additional medical cash plan scheme
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Company supported employee Health and Wellbeing programme
- Life assurance
- Free plentiful car parking and electrical car charging points
- Beautiful parkland setting with excellent transportation links to Cambridge, Milton Keynes and London

Right to Work

All candidates will be asked to provide proof of eligibility to work in the UK at interview.

Due to the requirements laid out by UK Visas and Immigration regarding Right to Work in the UK, SPD can only accept applications from individuals who currently have a status allowing them to work in the UK for this position.

We regret that we are unable to offer sponsorship for this role.

Equality

SPD is committed to providing a vibrant, ethical, and sustainable work environment that values equality, diversity, and inclusion.

If you require any reasonable adjustments to support you, at any stage during the application process, just let us know how we can help.
